learn.hook: What can make you as steady as a mountain and as calm as a still lake — without any gadgets? Yoga!
points: 'Yoga — A Way of Life' is an informative lesson about yoga and how it helps the body and mind.
The word 'yoga' comes from the Sanskrit root 'yuj', which means 'to join' or 'to unite' — joining body, breath and mind.
Yoga includes asanas (postures), pranayama (breathing exercises) and meditation (quietly focusing the mind).
Benefits: better flexibility, strength and balance, a calmer mind and better concentration.
International Day of Yoga is celebrated every year on 21 June. The United Nations declared it in 2014, and it was first celebrated in 2015.

example.q: Read: Every morning, Kavya unrolls her mat on the terrace. She begins with slow, deep breaths. Then she stands tall like a mountain and stretches like a tree. "Yoga makes my body flexible and my mind calm," she says. Since she started, she finds it easier to concentrate on her studies, and she rarely feels stiff after long hours at her desk. List two benefits of yoga that Kavya mentions or experiences.
steps: Kavya says yoga makes her body flexible.
She says it makes her mind calm.
She finds it easier to concentrate and rarely feels stiff.
example.answer: Any two: a flexible body, a calm mind, better concentration, less stiffness.

learn.reallife: Many schools hold a yoga session on 21 June, and lots of families begin their day with a few asanas and pranayama.

games.title: Yoga facts
items: International Day of Yoga is on 21 June.
It is celebrated every year on 21 June.
The word 'yoga' comes from a Sanskrit root meaning 'to join'.
Yoga can help improve balance and flexibility.
Regular practice builds balance and flexibility.

quiz.q: Where does Kavya do yoga in the passage?
quiz.explain: The passage says she unrolls her mat on the terrace.
steps: The setting is where Kavya does yoga.
The passage says she unrolls her mat on the terrace.
So she does yoga on the terrace.
Answer: on the terrace
quiz.mistake: Does not find the setting in the passage

quiz.q: How does Kavya begin her yoga practice?
quiz.explain: She begins with slow, deep breaths.
steps: Look at the first thing Kavya does.
She begins with slow, deep breaths.
Running, eating and music are not mentioned at the start.
Answer: with slow, deep breaths
quiz.mistake: Does not follow the order of actions

quiz.q: In the passage, Kavya "stands tall like a mountain". This is an example of:
quiz.explain: It compares her with a mountain using 'like'.
steps: 'Stands tall like a mountain' compares Kavya with a mountain.
A comparison using 'like' is a simile.
A metaphor would say she IS a mountain.
Answer: a simile
quiz.mistake: Forgets that 'like' signals a simile

quiz.q: What does 'flexible' mean?
quiz.explain: A flexible body can bend and stretch easily.
steps: A flexible body bends and stretches easily.
So 'flexible' means able to bend easily.
It is not about weight or sleep.
Answer: able to bend easily
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning

quiz.q: According to the passage, how has yoga helped Kavya with her studies?
options: She no longer needs to study
She finds it easier to concentrate
quiz.explain: The passage says she finds it easier to concentrate on her studies.
steps: The passage tells how yoga helps her studies.
It says she finds it easier to concentrate.
It does not say she gets every answer right.
Answer: She finds it easier to concentrate
quiz.mistake: Exaggerates what the passage says

quiz.q: The word 'yoga' comes from the Sanskrit root 'yuj'. What does 'yuj' mean?
quiz.explain: 'Yuj' means to join — yoga joins body, breath and mind.
steps: 'Yoga' comes from the Sanskrit root 'yuj'.
'Yuj' means to join or unite.
Yoga joins body, breath and mind.
Answer: to join or unite
quiz.mistake: Does not know the meaning of the root

quiz.q: On which date is International Day of Yoga celebrated?
quiz.explain: It is celebrated every year on 21 June.
steps: International Day of Yoga is celebrated every year.
Its date is 21 June.
15 August is Independence Day; 14 November is Children's Day.
Answer: 21 June
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with other important dates

quiz.q: What are 'asanas'?
quiz.explain: Asanas are the body positions practised in yoga.
steps: Yoga has postures and breathing exercises.
The body positions are called asanas.
Breathing exercises are pranayama.
Answer: yoga postures
quiz.mistake: Mixes up asanas with pranayama

teach.ask: Gappu stretches his wings: 'Everyone is doing yoga today! What is yoga, and how does it help?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Yoga joins body, breath and mind. It makes me flexible and calm. Namaste!
teach.nudge: Does yoga help only the body, or the mind too?

revise.summary: 'Yoga — A Way of Life' is an informative lesson about yoga and how it helps the body and mind. Yoga includes asanas, pranayama and meditation.
focus: Finding details and benefits of yoga from a passage
Meaning of 'yuj' and the parts of yoga
remember: 'Yoga' comes from the Sanskrit root 'yuj', meaning 'to join' or 'to unite'.
Asanas (postures), pranayama (breathing exercises), meditation (quietly focusing the mind).
International Day of Yoga is on 21 June; the UN declared it in 2014 and it was first celebrated in 2015.
Benefits: flexibility, strength, balance, a calmer mind, better concentration.
traps: Don't mix up asanas (postures) with pranayama (breathing).
Don't exaggerate what the passage says; it says she finds it easier to concentrate.
Don't call 'stands tall like a mountain' a metaphor; it is a simile because of 'like'.

learn.hook: Your body is like a phone: it needs charging (sleep), good fuel (food) and the right apps (exercise)!
points: A healthy lifestyle includes a balanced diet, regular exercise, enough sleep, cleanliness and a calm mind.
A balanced diet has the right amounts of different foods: grains, pulses, vegetables, fruits, milk products and water.
Instructions (like yoga steps) are written as imperative sentences that start with a verb: 'Stand straight.' 'Breathe in slowly.'
Sequence words make instructions clear: first, next, then, after that, finally.
Safety in yoga: practise on a mat with an empty or light stomach, learn from a trained teacher, and never force a pose that hurts.

example.q: Think it through: Turn this into instructions for the tree pose (Vrikshasana): stand straight; raise one foot to the inside of the other leg; join palms; hold; come back.
steps: Begin each step with a verb.
Add sequence words.
Keep it simple and safe.
example.answer: First, stand straight. Next, place your right foot on the inside of your left leg (not on the knee). Then join your palms. Hold and breathe. Finally, lower your foot and repeat on the other side.

learn.reallife: Recipes, game rules and science-activity steps are all written as imperative instructions with sequence words.

games.title: Tree pose steps
games.prompt: Put the tree pose steps in order
items: Shift your weight onto your left leg.
Place your right foot on the inside of your left leg.
Join your palms and hold, breathing gently.
Lower your foot and repeat with the other leg.

quiz.q: Which is part of a healthy lifestyle?
quiz.explain: Exercise and sleep keep the body and mind healthy.
steps: A healthy lifestyle keeps body and mind healthy.
Regular exercise and enough sleep do this.
Late nights, only sweets and staying indoors do not.
Answer: regular exercise and enough sleep
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise healthy habits

quiz.q: What is a balanced diet?
options: eating as much as you like
food with the right amounts of different food groups
quiz.explain: A balanced diet includes grains, pulses, vegetables, fruit, milk products and water.
steps: A balanced diet has many food groups.
It includes grains, pulses, vegetables, fruit, milk products and water in the right amounts.
One kind of food alone is not balanced.
Answer: food with the right amounts of different food groups
quiz.mistake: Thinks one kind of food is enough

quiz.q: Which sentence is an instruction (imperative)?
quiz.explain: Imperative sentences give a command or instruction and usually begin with a verb.
steps: An imperative sentence gives an instruction and usually begins with a verb.
'Breathe in slowly.' begins with the verb 'Breathe'.
The others are a statement, a question and an exclamation.
Answer: Breathe in slowly.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a statement with an instruction

quiz.q: Which word shows the last step in instructions?
quiz.explain: 'Finally' signals the last step.
steps: Sequence words show the order of steps: first, next, then, finally.
'Finally' marks the last step.
'First' marks the beginning.
Answer: finally
quiz.mistake: Does not know sequence words

quiz.q: What is the safe way to do a difficult yoga pose?
options: Force your body into the pose
Copy it quickly from a video without care
Do it right after a heavy meal
Learn from a trained teacher and stop if it hurts
quiz.explain: Yoga should never be forced; a trained teacher keeps you safe.
steps: Yoga should never be forced.
A trained teacher can guide you, and you must stop if it hurts.
Forcing or copying carelessly can cause injury.
Answer: Learn from a trained teacher and stop if it hurts
quiz.mistake: Thinks pain means progress

quiz.q: In the tree pose, where should the raised foot NOT be placed?
options: at the inner ankle, toes on the floor
quiz.explain: Pressing on the knee joint can hurt it; the foot goes above or below the knee.
steps: In the tree pose, the foot goes above or below the knee.
Pressing on the knee joint can hurt it.
So the foot should NOT be placed directly on the knee.
Answer: directly on the knee
quiz.mistake: Does not know the safety point

quiz.q: Which is the best order for the first two steps of the tree pose?
options: Lift your foot, then stand straight
Stand straight, then shift your weight onto one leg
quiz.explain: You first stand steady, then shift your weight before lifting a foot.
steps: You need balance before lifting a foot.
First stand straight, then shift your weight onto one leg.
Lifting the foot first would make you unsteady.
Answer: Stand straight, then shift your weight onto one leg
quiz.mistake: Does not think about the logical order of steps

quiz.q: Which habit helps keep germs away?
options: washing hands with soap before eating
quiz.explain: Washing hands with soap removes germs.
steps: Germs on hands can get into food.
Washing hands with soap before eating removes them.
Sharing handkerchiefs and biting nails spread germs.
Answer: washing hands with soap before eating
quiz.mistake: Does not connect cleanliness with health

teach.ask: Gappu yawns at midnight with a bag of chips: 'Am I living a healthy life?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Good sleep, healthy food and exercise — no more midnight chips for me!
teach.nudge: What about my food and my sleep — what should I change?

revise.summary: A healthy lifestyle includes a balanced diet, regular exercise, enough sleep, cleanliness and a calm mind. Instructions are written as imperative sentences with sequence words.
focus: Parts of a healthy lifestyle and a balanced diet
Writing instructions with imperatives and sequence words
remember: A balanced diet has grains, pulses, vegetables, fruits, milk products and water in the right amounts.
Instructions start with a verb: 'Stand straight.' 'Breathe in slowly.'
Sequence words: first, next, then, after that, finally.
Practise yoga on a mat with an empty or light stomach, learn from a trained teacher, and never force a pose that hurts.
traps: Pain does not mean progress; stop if a pose hurts.
In the tree pose, don't place the raised foot directly on the knee.
One kind of food is not enough for a balanced diet.

learn.hook: Some sentences tell, some ask, some order and some shout with joy. Can you tell which is which?
points: A declarative (assertive) sentence makes a statement and ends with a full stop: 'Yoga keeps us fit.'
An interrogative sentence asks a question and ends with a question mark: 'Do you practise yoga?'
An imperative sentence gives a command, request or instruction: 'Stand straight.' 'Please close the door.'
An exclamatory sentence shows strong feeling and ends with an exclamation mark: 'What a lovely morning!'
In imperative sentences the subject 'you' is usually understood, not written.

example.q: Think it through: Identify each: (a) Breathe in deeply. (b) How calm I feel! (c) Is yoga easy? (d) Kavya does yoga daily.
steps: (a) gives an instruction → imperative.
(b) shows strong feeling → exclamatory.
(c) asks → interrogative.
(d) states a fact → declarative.

learn.reallife: Notice them in daily life: 'Close the door.' (imperative), 'Where's my bag?' (interrogative), 'What a goal!' (exclamatory).

quiz.q: What kind of sentence is 'Stand straight and breathe slowly.'?
quiz.explain: It gives an instruction, so it is imperative.
steps: The sentence gives an instruction.
Sentences that give commands or instructions are imperative.
It is not a question or a strong feeling.
Answer: imperative
quiz.mistake: Thinks every sentence with a full stop is declarative

quiz.q: Which is an interrogative sentence?
options: Do you do yoga every morning?
How fresh I feel after yoga!
quiz.explain: It asks a question and ends with a question mark.
steps: An interrogative sentence asks a question.
'Do you do yoga every morning?' asks a question and ends with '?'.
The others state, instruct or exclaim.
Answer: Do you do yoga every morning?
quiz.mistake: Does not notice the question form

quiz.q: Which is an exclamatory sentence?
options: What a wonderful pose that is!
quiz.explain: It expresses strong feeling and ends with '!'.
steps: An exclamatory sentence shows strong feeling and ends with '!'.
'What a wonderful pose that is!' does this.
'That is a wonderful pose.' is a statement.
Answer: What a wonderful pose that is!
quiz.mistake: Confuses strong feeling with a statement

quiz.q: Which mark ends a declarative sentence?
quiz.explain: Statements end with a full stop.
steps: A declarative sentence makes a statement.
Statements end with a full stop.
Questions end with '?', exclamations with '!'.
Answer: full stop
quiz.mistake: Mixes up punctuation for sentence types

quiz.q: In 'Please pass the salt', who is the understood subject?
quiz.explain: Imperative sentences speak to 'you', which is usually not written.
steps: Imperative sentences speak directly to someone.
The understood subject is 'you'.
'Please pass the salt' means '(You) please pass the salt'.
Answer: you
quiz.mistake: Thinks imperatives have no subject at all

quiz.q: Change to an interrogative: 'Kavya practises yoga daily.'
quiz.explain: Use 'Does' + subject + base verb: Does Kavya practise...?
steps: Questions in the present use Do/Does + subject + base verb.
Kavya is one person, so 'Does'; the verb drops its -s: practise.
So: Does Kavya practise yoga daily?
Answer: Does Kavya practise yoga daily?
quiz.mistake: Keeps the -s on the verb after 'does'

quiz.q: 'How flexible you are!' is:
quiz.explain: Although it starts with 'How', it shows strong feeling and ends with '!'.
steps: 'How flexible you are!' starts with 'How' but asks nothing.
It shows strong feeling and ends with '!'.
So it is exclamatory.
Answer: exclamatory
quiz.mistake: Thinks every sentence starting with 'How' is a question

quiz.q: Which sentence is declarative?
options: Did yoga begin in ancient India?
What an ancient practice yoga is!
quiz.explain: It makes a statement and ends with a full stop.
steps: A declarative sentence states a fact and ends with a full stop.
'Yoga began in ancient India.' does this.
The others ask, instruct or exclaim.
Answer: Yoga began in ancient India.
quiz.mistake: Does not identify a plain statement

teach.ask: Gappu chirps: 'My teacher says there are four kinds of sentences. How do I tell them apart?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Tell, ask, order, exclaim — four kinds of sentences. What fun this is!
teach.nudge: What kind of sentence gives an order or instruction?

revise.summary: There are four kinds of sentences: declarative, interrogative, imperative and exclamatory. Each has its own job and end mark.
focus: Identifying the four kinds of sentences
Changing a statement into a question
remember: Declarative (assertive): makes a statement, ends with a full stop.
Interrogative: asks a question, ends with a question mark.
Imperative: gives a command, request or instruction; the subject 'you' is usually understood.
Exclamatory: shows strong feeling, ends with an exclamation mark.
traps: Not every sentence with a full stop is declarative; 'Stand straight.' is imperative.
Not every sentence starting with 'How' is a question: 'How flexible you are!' is exclamatory.
Don't keep the -s after 'does': 'Does Kavya practise...?', not 'Does Kavya practises...?'
